answer_1.quote: We evaluate our best‑performing MEDIT model ... human evaluation ... proficient linguists (and native language speakers) ... to ensure they meet the instructional task‑specific constraints across the various languages ...
answer_1.outputs: Edited sentences produced by the model according to the given instruction

answer_2.quote: We use the MaxMatch (M2) Scorer, ERRANT, GLEU for GEC; SARI and BLEU for simplification; Self‑BLEU and mUSE for paraphrasing.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluations of the model outputs by proficient linguists (and native language speakers) ... rating the quality of the output on three criteria: fluency, adequacy, and accuracy.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each output on fluency (grammaticality and naturalness), adequacy (meaning preservation), and accuracy (whether the desired edits were made).
